The degree counts in Fig. 1d show k = 4 nodes making up 4.6–17.7% of branch points across the six datasets. The pooled 16.6% is 96% human-neuron nodes. Bifurcation angles also fail to peak at 2π/3. | [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md) v3 | Scaffolding individuality: coordination, cooperation, collaboration and community | Griesemer & Shavit (2023), DOI-10.1098/rstb.2021.0398. The paper sets out an idealized three-stage sequence of interaction types, which it calls a "first and rough sketch" (§1). Stage 1 is coordination in *collections* (pairwise, "aggregative" interactions of co-located individuals). Stage 2 is cooperation in *conexuses* (a connected web of binary interactions whose benefits can still be counted per member). Stage 3 is collaboration in *communities*: heterogeneous multi-way interactions around a shared goal, in which generatively entrenched "core" interactions give organizational closure. Table 1 puts the transition to a new level of individuality between stages 2 and 3 only. The paper asserts, rather than argues, that this describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity. Its one argued conclusion is hedged: community-level inheritance "seem[s] likely to evolve in tandem" with community-level individuality (§3). | Proposed — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)); a short programmatic sketch, and the authors call it one. It is worth knowing as the compact statement of Griesemer's scaffolding, reproducer and generative-entrenchment view applied to human social transitions. Its headline claims (non-circularity; individuality as a special case of collectivity) appear only in the abstract. Two things would settle it: the model of community "reliability" and endogenization the authors promise in §2 ("We hope to explore such models in future work"), or an application of the 3Cs to a worked case, such as the companion Neolithic paper, that separates collection, conexus and community by measurable criteria. |
